name: Pastel Orange
lede: Pastel Orange is ColorHub's English name for Kanzō-iro, a vivid orange that Japanese tradition names for the daylily, and the name also independently turns up as a plated hue in Ridgway's 1912 color standard.

sections.title: A daylily, independently plated
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Kanzō-iro (萱草色), "daylily-colored," after the orange flowers of the daylily (Hemerocallis) [1]. Despite the English name ColorHub carries, this is in fact a vivid, fully saturated orange, not a pale pastel [1][2]. The name is a mismatch the library notes rather than silently corrects [1]. The same hue range is independently plated in Ridgway's 1912 standard, plate II, hue 11, a scan of an aged plate read as approximate [2]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places it in block 48, "moderate orange," about 3.2 units from that block's centre [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 67, chroma 75, hue 58 degrees: a bright, highly saturated orange[2]. The library's nearest other named colors are [[dusty-orange]], [[heat-wave]] and [[cadmium-orange]], each within 4 units [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in only 5 of 23,781 paintings, a vanishingly small fraction, as photographed [3]. With so few matches our data cannot support claims about painters or role patterns with any confidence; the honest finding is simply that this vivid an orange is rare across the archive's six centuries of painting [3]. The earliest match is a 1528 Adam by Lucas Cranach the Elder, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
